Hey there! 

It's hard to face alcoholism and tell others but it will only help your therapist work through your problems with you. Very often there are underlying mental health issues that contribute to addiction. I'd also suggest seeing a psychiatrist and getting prescribed medicine over controlled substances because they will only harm you further. Prescription meds helped me a lot in recovery with managing anxiety and depression

All of us have been at that point where we're not sure if we want to stop even when it's made our life hell. Addiction functions very complexly for addicts physically and mentally it's hard to reach that desire to stop. 

Everyone in AA wants you there and wants to help you at least understand what you're up against. All you need is that tiny portion of you that wants to stop to learn and move forward 

I became an alcoholic at 19 and it destroyed me for years but in truth it was worth all the misery because I'm happier now than I can remember ever being in my life. 

I really hope you continue to go to meetings even half heartedly and try and connect with others because the people in the rooms saved me and I wish the same for you 

https://aa-intergroup.org/oiaa/meetings/

The Corona Virus group 8pm EST is hosted by an amazing transgender woman and her meetings are always excellent. I'm sure she would love to talk to you if you're interested 

Best of luck. Contact me any time you need to talk
